parole.significato: A pickle made from grated unripe papaya, popular in the Philippines.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Philippine Spanish achara, possibly from Malay acar, ultimately from Classical Persian آچار (āčār, “pickle, marinade”). Compare Tagalog atsara, Cebuano atsara, Hiligaynon atsara, Indonesian acar, Hindi अचार (acār). Doublet of acar, achar, and atsara.

parole.significato: A canoe; an outrigger canoe or dugout.
parole.testo: From Philippine Spanish banca, from Tagalog bangka.

parole.significato: A small dugout canoe boat from the Philippines, which normally lacks outriggers and is usually used in calm waters.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Philippine Spanish baroto.

parole.significato: A long, heavy, single-edged machete.
parole.testo: From Philippine Spanish bolo, from Tagalog bolo.

parole.significato: A small eatery or canteen or cafeteria that serves local (usually Filipino) food
parole.testo: From Philippine Spanish carindería, where the root, Spanish carí, itself is from Tagalog kari (“curry”). Compare Tagalog karinderya.

parole.significato: A light two-wheeled, horse-drawn passenger carriage with a tilt roof used to convey passengers within city limits or fo…
parole.testo: From Philippine Spanish carromata, from Spanish carromato + -a. Compare Tagalog karomata, Cebuano karomata.

parole.significato: A name for the various dance rituals and celebrations of the Igorot people.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Philippine Spanish cañao.

parole.significato: The soursop (Annona muricata) (tree and fruit).
parole.testo: Borrowed from Philippine Spanish guayábano (“soursop”), as in Spanish guanábano (“soursop tree”) with possible influence from Spanish guayaba (“guava”), from Taíno wanaban.

parole.significato: An educated wealthy and elite Filipino during the Spanish colonial period of the Philippines.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Philippine Spanish ilustrado.

parole.significato: Synonym of Tausug (“member of a people”).
parole.testo: Borrowed from Philippine Spanish joloano, from Joló + -ano.

parole.significato: A Moro swordsman who attacked and killed occupying and invading police and soldiers, expecting to be killed himself.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Philippine Spanish juramentado.

parole.significato: A kind of persimmon tree (Diospyros blancoi) from the Philippine Islands, now introduced into the East and West Indies.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Philippine Spanish mabolo, from Tagalog mabulo.

parole.significato: Filipino coconut pudding dessert
parole.testo: From Philippine Spanish maja blanca, from maja + blanca (“white”). Related to Spanish manjar blanco (literally “white delicacy”). Compare Tagalog maha-blangka, French blanc-manger.

parole.significato: A person of mixed Spanish Filipino and ethnic Austronesian Filipino ancestry (especially during the Spanish colonial pe…
parole.testo: From Philippine Spanish mestizo de español, from mestizo (“mixed”) + de (“of”) + español (“Spanish”).

parole.significato: A person of mixed ethnic Chinese Filipino and Austronesian Filipino ancestry (especially during the Spanish colonial pe…
parole.testo: From Philippine Spanish mestizo de sangley, from mestizo (“mixed”) + de (“of”) + sangley (“Chinese”).

parole.significato: A member of a class of several ethnic groups who inhabit isolated parts of Southeast Asia.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Philippine Spanish negrito (“short dark-skinned person”), from negro (“black person; dark-skinned person”) + -ito (“small; short; little”, diminutive suffix).

parole.significato: Filipino noodles
parole.testo: Borrowed from Philippine Spanish pancit, from Hokkien. See more info at Spanish pancit. Compare Tagalog pansit, Indonesian pangsit.

parole.significato: A Filipino dish of stir-fried egg noodles with meat, vegetables, soy sauce and other seasonings.
parole.testo: From Philippine Spanish pancit cantón, where Philippine Spanish pancit is from Hokkien, while Spanish Cantón is ultimately from Mandarin 廣東 /广东 (Guǎngdōng), possibly via Portuguese Cantão.

parole.significato: A restaurant that serves pancit noodles.
parole.testo: From Philippine Spanish pancitería. Compare Tagalog pansiterya.

parole.significato: A sailing vessel found in the waters of the Philippines, similar to a proa.
parole.testo: From Philippine Spanish parao, from Cebuano paraw.

parole.significato: Dental filling.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Philippine Spanish pasta, from Late Latin pasta (“dough, pastry cake, paste”), from Ancient Greek παστά (pastá, “barley porridge”). Doublet of paste.

parole.significato: Arabian jasmine (Jasminum sambac).
parole.testo: Borrowed from Philippine Spanish sampaguita, from sampaga + -ita.

parole.significato: A person of pure ethnic Chinese ancestry (especially during the Spanish colonial period in the Philippines)
parole.testo: From Philippine Spanish Sangley, ultimately from Hokkien.

parole.significato: A fish bowl or barrel-shaped container where balls used in a raffle or a lottery are placed. In the case of a raffle, t…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Philippine Spanish tambiolo, from tambo + -i- + Italian -olo. See also Spanish tómbola, which is also from Italian tombola. Compare Tagalog tambiyolo.

parole.significato: Swamp ricegrass, Leersia hexandra, a grass cultivated for green forage.
parole.testo: From Philippine Spanish zacate, from Mexican Spanish zacate, from Classical Nahuatl zacatl (“dry weeds or grass; fodder, forage”), from Uto-Aztecan *saka-t.
